Analysts project billions of dollars in sales, while Take-Two investors will be watching to see whether the highly anticipated game can live up to sky-high expectations. sample.title: Myanmar committed genocide against its Rohingya minority, UN's top court rules | BBC News
sample.description:
The International Court of Justice (ICJ) has ruled that Myanmar committed genocide against its Rohingya minority population in northern Rakhine state.
 
In 2017, a military crackdown killed thousands of Rohingya - a Muslim ethnic minority - and forced more than 700,000 to flee Buddhist-majority Myanmar for neighbouring Bangladesh.
 
Judge Yuji Iwasawa says there is a "reasonable inference that Myanmar security forces acted with genocidal intent", and Myanmar had the "intention to destroy" a substantial part of the Rohingya.
 
Myanmar had denied genocide in the case brought by The Gambia.

Are homes at risk from flooded mines? | BBC News
sample.description:
Communities around the UK could face the same fate as a flooded Welsh village if work is not done to manage the risk of underground mine water, the BBC has been told. 

Families in south Wales whose homes were submerged by a torrent of mine water after a quarry blast said they now fear their children could be caught in another flood. 

With a quarter of people in the UK living above old mines, experts in flood risk management and mines have said more needs to be done to assess the risk from flooding and protect families and their homes. 

The UK Government said there is no "national assessment" of the risks posed by flooded mines, although various bodies do have responsibility for some mines. 

The owner of the quarry in Wales, Breedon, said it recognised the distress the flood caused but said it was an isolated incident following a project that was years in the planning. It added it is cooperating fully with the HSE investigation.
